description: Composite figure group; only three panels are supplied (d, e, f), while the caption also describes (a) a depth-of-penetration vs indentation load (p-h) plot, (b) an optical micrograph of the indent on the SPSed HES sample and (c) a compressive engineering stress-strain curve. (d) is a filled pentagonal radar (spider) diagram whose five radial axes are labelled "Compressive Strain (%)" with ticks 6/12/18/24, "Compressive Stress (MPa)" with ticks 600/1200/1800/2400, "Elastic modulus (GPa)" with ticks 50/100/150/200, plus a vertical top axis with ticks 20/40/60/80/100 and a right axis with blue ticks 2/4/6/8/10, both untitled; two overlaid polygons (green and purple) are plotted. (e) scatters Microhardness (GPa, 0–9) against Density (g/cc, 6.0–8.5): a dark-blue star labelled "Present Work" sits near 6.7 g/cc and just below 8 GPa, isolated above all literature points by pink dashed guides at about 7 GPa and 6.8 g/cc. (f) scatters Compressive Strength (MPa, 800–2200) against Density (g/cc, 6.0–8.5), the "Present Work" star at about 6.5 g/cc and ~2060 MPa being the highest of the plotted set. Together the panels argue that this low-density HES combines high hardness and high compressive strength at low density, outperforming conventional steels and other HEAs.

Two overlaid closed polygons (one green, one purple) summarise the SPSed pellet's physical and mechanical properties; no numeric values for the polygons are printed.

Legend entries on the right: [21] purple circle, [22] blue circle, [26] green triangle, [59] open hexagon, [61] teal circle, [63] open magenta triangle, [64] dark-red square, [65] dark-red square.

Scatter plot of Compressive Strength (MPa, y-axis 800–2200) versus Density (g/cc, x-axis 6.0–8.5). The blue star labelled 'Present Work' at about 6.5 g/cc and ~2060 MPa is the highest point shown. Legend entries: [14] yellow square, [22] blue circle, [60] open red square, [62] green triangle, [63] dark-red square, [66] dark-blue hexagon; literature points span roughly 850–2000 MPa over 7.0–8.3 g/cc.

observations.observation: Panel (d) is a filled pentagonal radar/spider diagram with five radial axes and two overlaid closed polygons, one drawn in green and one in purple/violet.

The radar diagram (d) labels three axes: 'Compressive Strain (%)' (ticks 6, 12, 18, 24), 'Compressive Stress (MPa)' (ticks 600, 1200, 1800, 2400) and 'Elastic modulus (GPa)' (ticks 50, 100, 150, 200).

Two radial axes of (d) carry no title in the image: the vertical top axis with ticks 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 and the right-hand axis with blue ticks 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, so the quantities they represent cannot be identified from the pixels.
Panel (e) is a scatter plot of Microhardness (GPa, y 0–9) against Density (g/cc, x 6.0–8.5).

In (e) a dark-blue star labelled 'Present Work' is plotted at about 6.7 g/cc and just below 8 GPa, with dashed pink guide lines at approximately 7 GPa (horizontal) and 6.8 g/cc (vertical); every other point lies below the 7 GPa line.

The legend of (e) lists literature references [21] purple circle, [22] blue circle, [26] green triangle, [59] open hexagon, [61] teal circle, [63] open magenta triangle, [64] dark-red square and [65] dark-red square.
Panel (f) is a scatter plot of Compressive Strength (MPa, y 800–2200) against Density (g/cc, x 6.0–8.5).

In (f) the 'Present Work' blue star at about 6.5 g/cc and ~2060 MPa is the highest compressive-strength point in the panel; the remaining literature points fall roughly between 850 and 2000 MPa at 7.0–8.3 g/cc.
The legend of (f) lists references [14] yellow square, [22] blue circle, [60] open red square, [62] green triangle, [63] dark-red square and [66] dark-blue hexagon.

The caption states that (a) is a depth of penetration vs indentation load (p-h) plot, (b) an optical micrograph of the indent on the SPSed HES sample, and (c) a compressive engineering stress-strain curve; these three panels are not present in the supplied images.

The caption states that (e) and (f) compare microhardness vs density and ultimate compressive stress vs density of the present work with conventional steel and other HEAs, with details listed in supplementary Table S1.
The citing text reports an indentation depth of ~5.08 μm for the SPSed samples and states that the nature of the p-h curve indicates limited plasticity.
The citing text reports average microhardness of approximately 7.8 ± 0.3 GPa and elastic modulus of approximately 184 ± 5 GPa for the SPSed pellet.
The citing text reports average ultimate compressive stress of 2046 ± 160 MPa and compressive strain of 19% for the SPSed pellet.

The citing text states that (b) shows no evidence of crack formation in the optical image of the indent even at a load of 5000 mN, and that ferritic dual-phase steel has microhardness of 2.0–2.4 GPa, far below the 7.8 GPa of the present alloy.
